policies.title: Software Change Standard
policies.description: Baseline standards for software modifications, acceptance criteria, dependency additions, configuration, and documentation.

controls.name: Acceptance Criteria Definition
controls.description: Changes must satisfy explicit functional acceptance criteria documented in pull request context.

controls.name: Bounded Change Scope
controls.description: Modifications must be bounded to the declared feature scope with no extraneous or unrelated refactoring.

controls.name: Dependency Justification
controls.description: New package dependencies must be minimal, secure, maintained, and justified in the change.

controls.name: Environment Configuration Isolation
controls.description: Configuration values and endpoints must use environment variables rather than hardcoded literals.

controls.name: Documentation Maintenance
controls.description: Public APIs, user-facing features, or operational procedures must update associated documentation.

policies.title: Secure Coding Standard
policies.description: Mandatory secure coding practices including input validation, server-side authorisation, secret prevention, and sanitised error delivery.

controls.name: External Input Validation
controls.description: All external data entering server boundaries must undergo strict schema validation before processing.

controls.name: Server-Side Authorisation
controls.description: Protected resources and write operations must enforce server-side identity and permission checks.

controls.name: No Committed Secrets
controls.description: Source code and git commits must never contain credentials, API keys, tokens, or sensitive certificates.

controls.name: Safe Error Responses
controls.description: Server error responses returned to clients must never leak internal stack traces or database details.

controls.name: Safe Query and Command Execution
controls.description: Database queries and system commands must use parameterised interfaces preventing injection.

policies.title: Testing Standard
policies.description: Requirements for automated testing, happy path validation, negative/error condition coverage, and regression prevention.

controls.name: Automated Test Requirement
controls.description: All functional code changes must include corresponding automated unit or integration tests.

controls.name: Happy Path Test Coverage
controls.description: Tests must exercise the successful execution paths and verify expected outputs or state changes.

controls.name: Negative and Error Path Coverage
controls.description: Tests must explicitly cover failure states, invalid inputs, rejection boundaries, and error codes.

controls.name: Regression Suite Integrity
controls.description: Changes must preserve existing test suite integrity without deleting or disabling existing tests.

policies.title: HTTP API Standard
policies.description: Standards for REST/HTTP endpoints, method semantics, HTTP status codes, structured envelopes, and error formatting.

controls.name: Semantic HTTP Methods
controls.description: Endpoints must use semantic HTTP verbs (GET for retrieval, POST for creation, PUT/PATCH for update, DELETE for removal).

controls.name: Explicit Status Codes
controls.description: Responses must emit explicit, standard HTTP status codes (e.g. 200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 500).

controls.name: Structured JSON Envelopes
controls.description: Payloads returned by API routes must be consistent JSON structures with defined schemas.

controls.name: Request Payload Validation
controls.description: HTTP request bodies and query parameters must be validated using schema parsing before business logic execution.

controls.name: Internal Stack and Detail Redaction
controls.description: 5xx responses must emit generic fault descriptions and withhold low-level runtime exceptions from clients.

policies.title: Frontend Quality Standard
policies.description: Accessibility, keyboard navigation, user feedback states, responsive design, and dual validation standards for web user interfaces.

controls.name: Accessible Form Labels
controls.description: All interactive inputs must have programmatic, associated accessible labels via htmlFor or aria-label.

controls.name: Keyboard Navigability
controls.description: All interactive elements must be focusable, operable via keyboard, and maintain visible focus styles.

controls.name: Explicit Feedback States
controls.description: Forms and asynchronous actions must present clear loading, success, and error feedback states to users.

controls.name: Responsive Layout Support
controls.description: User interfaces must adapt gracefully across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports without clipping content.

controls.name: Dual Client and Server Validation
controls.description: Client-side form validation may provide immediate guidance, but server-side validation remains authoritative.

policies.title: Observability and Errors Standard
policies.description: Operational requirements for deliberate error handling, log sanitisation, structured telemetry, client timeouts, and retry limits.

controls.name: Deliberate Error Handling
controls.description: Operations subject to failure must use structured try/catch blocks or result types without unhandled promise rejections.

controls.name: Sanitised Logging
controls.description: Log records must be scrubbed of credentials, authentication headers, tokens, and personal identifiable information.

controls.name: Structured Diagnostic Logs
controls.description: Log outputs must include structured context (such as action names, error codes, and correlation identifiers).

controls.name: Remote Client Timeouts
controls.description: Outbound HTTP or RPC network calls must configure explicit execution timeouts using AbortController or client options.

controls.name: Bounded Retry Loops
controls.description: Retry mechanisms must be bounded with maximum attempt counts and backoff strategies to prevent stampedes.

policies.title: Application Data Handling Standard
policies.description: Rules for classifying application data, enforcing data minimisation, protecting personal data in transit/logs, and documenting retention.

controls.name: Data Field Classification
controls.description: Data payloads handling user information must identify and classify fields by sensitivity (e.g. public, internal, personal).

controls.name: Data Minimisation
controls.description: Forms and APIs must only collect data fields strictly necessary for the immediate business function.

controls.name: No Sensitive Data in Logs
controls.description: Email addresses, customer identifiers, contact details, and credentials must never appear in application logs.

controls.name: Retention and Storage Documentation
controls.description: Persistent data models must specify retention criteria and intended persistence mechanisms.

controls.name: Third-Party Data Egress Notice
controls.description: Transmission of customer or application data to external third-party services must be declared and reviewed.
